name: Indian D2C brands (Shopify / WooCommerce)
icp: Indian direct-to-consumer brands doing roughly ₹50 lakh to ₹50 crore a year online, selling via their own Shopify/WooCommerce store with COD orders, founder-led. Categories like fashion, beauty, food, home, wellness.
disqualifiers: Marketplace-only sellers with no own store
Large brands with in-house tech teams (e.g. listed companies)
Agencies, aggregators or dropshipping stores with no real brand

pains.solution: WhatsApp COD confirmation + address verification flow that cancels or nudges risky orders before dispatch
pains.evidence_to_look_for: COD offered, Shopify store, ads-driven traffic

pains.pain: Support team answering the same 'where is my order' and return questions on WhatsApp/Instagram
pains.solution: WhatsApp/Instagram support agent in Hinglish connected to Shopify and the shipping aggregator, handing off edge cases
pains.evidence_to_look_for: WhatsApp chat button, support email only, hiring support executives

pains.solution: Personalized WhatsApp cart recovery with offers tuned by product and customer history
pains.evidence_to_look_for: No visible WhatsApp marketing, high-AOV products

offer: A 2-week setup of WhatsApp COD confirmation + order-status support on their store
guarantee: If RTO or support load doesn't measurably drop in 30 days, no monthly fee
mystery_shop: Message the brand's WhatsApp asking 'where is my order' style questions and time the reply
Add to cart, leave, and see whether any recovery message arrives
tone: Founder-to-founder, crisp, Indian business English, talks in RTO %, ₹ and orders/day.
language_notes: WhatsApp message should be short and only intended for after the first contact (email/LinkedIn/intro). Never suggest cold WhatsApp blasts.
